title: Customs and Other Legislation Amendment (Illicit Tobacco Enforcement Modernisation and Other Measures) Bill 2026
short_title: Customs and Other Legislation Amendment (Illicit Tobacco Enforcement Modernisation and Other Measures) Bill 2026

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create additional illicit tobacco offences, change customs enforcement and licensing arrangements, and amend powers for investigating and recovering proceeds of crime.

New offences would address tobacco imports, possession and movement involving reasonable suspicion of unlawful importation or revenue fraud, alongside offences concerning missing import permissions or breached conditions.
Most measures would begin the day after Royal Assent, with licensing changes starting by proclamation or automatically after the prescribed 12-month period expires.
changes: Customs control would extend over duty-refunded tobacco until export, sale or specified refund application outcomes.
The process for claiming return of seized illicit tobacco would be removed.
Production orders could be sought after proceedings start and reach documents located in or accessible from Australia.
Unexplained wealth calculations would avoid counting property traced to one source multiple times.
Pecuniary penalty order reductions would reflect amounts actually paid rather than amounts merely payable.
summary.affected: Tobacco importers, carriers, freight forwarders, customs brokers, retailers and operators of depots and warehouses, and people liable under pecuniary penalty orders, are affected.
